description:
The National Museum of the Legion of Honour and Orders of Chivalry in Paris explores the history of honours and decorations. Its collections connect insignia with the people, institutions and ceremonies behind them.

Paintings, weapons, costumes, documents and decorative objects place French and international orders within a wider account of public recognition and political history.

description:
The Maison Bonaparte in Ajaccio preserves the family home associated with Napoleon’s childhood. Given to the French state in 1923, it forms a setting for exploring the Bonaparte family’s Corsican history.

Furniture, paintings, prints and family material connect domestic life with the Mediterranean world of the eighteenth century and the family’s later historical significance.

description:
The National Maritime Museum’s Paris collection explores the relationship between France and the sea. It forms part of a museum network with further sites on the French coast.

Ship models, marine painting, decorative sculpture and naval historical objects connect shipbuilding and navigation with commerce, state power and maritime life.
